The _Warcraft_ universe is a high-fantasy franchise developed by Blizzard Entertainment . Set in the richly detailed world of Azeroth and beyond , the main storyline revolves around the conflicts between diverse races such as humans , orcs , elves , and the undead . The original game, _Warcraft: Orcs & Humans_ , released in 1994, pioneered the real-time strategy (RTS) genre. It was followed by sequels and expansions , including _Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness_ and _Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos_ .

excerpts:
Put your stuff in the frame just like you would normally.  
  
You then need to define certain fields. To keep to the example in the thread linked I'll pretend panel is my options frame.  
  
panel.name must be defined. It would be helpful if its the name of your addon but I imagine wow has no idea. You could put any string here.  
  
After that, the rest are optional.  
  
panel.okay is the function that will happen when you click ok. IE: you push the changed variables to the ones your addon will use.  
  
panel.cancel is the function that will happen when you click cancel.  
  
panel.default is the function that will happen when you click default.  
  
You need to call the function InterfaceOptions\_AddCategory(panel) to push your panel on the list of those Blizzard will recognize.  
  
It really is that easy.

-- Once a frame is ready to be used as a panel, it must be registered using the function
-- InterfaceOptions_AddCategory, i.e. InterfaceOptions_AddCategory(panel)
--
-- Panels can be designated as sub-categories of existing options. These panels are listed
-- with smaller text, offset, and tied to parent categories. The parent categories can be expanded
-- or collapsed to toggle display of their sub-categories.
--
-- When players select a category of options from the Interface Options frame, the panel associated
-- with that category will be anchored to the right hand side of the Interface Options frame and shown.
--
-- The following members and methods are used by the Interface Options frame to display and organize panels.
--
-- panel.name - string (required)	
--	The name of the AddOn or group of configuration options. 
--	This is the text that will display in the AddOn options list.
--
-- panel.parent - string (optional)
--	Name of the parent of the AddOn or group of configuration options. 
--	This identifies "panel" as the child of another category.
--	If the parent category doesn't exist, "panel" will be displayed as a regular category.
--
-- panel.okay - function (optional)
--	This method will run when the player clicks "okay" in the Interface Options. 
--
-- panel.cancel - function (optional)
--	This method will run when the player clicks "cancel" in the Interface Options. 
--	Use this to revert their changes.
--
-- panel.default - function (optional)
--	This method will run when the player clicks "defaults". 
--	Use this to revert their changes to your defaults.
--

# How to Ditch Those Pesky Floating Names in World of Warcraft

Want to declutter your screen and focus on the glorious chaos of battle in **World of Warcraft**? Getting rid of those floating names is a key step. The quickest way to do it is to hit **Esc > Interface > Names** and uncheck the boxes corresponding to the nameplates you want to hide.
This is your first line of defense against nameplate overload!

## Diving Deeper: Mastering Nameplate Control

While the basic method works, there’s a universe of customization beyond just checking or unchecking boxes. Let’s explore the art of nameplate mastery, empowering you to create the perfect WoW viewing experience.

### The Blizzard Interface: Your Foundation

Before diving into addons, let’s maximize the built-in tools.

* **Enemy, Friendly, and Unit Types:** The **Interface > Names** panel allows you to toggle nameplates for enemies, friendly players, friendly NPCs, and even specific unit types like totems or pets. Experiment!

### 2\. I only want to see nameplates for enemies I’m actively targeting. How do I set that up?

In the default Blizzard interface, go to **Interface > Names** and make sure “Combat Only” is checked. Also, experiment with the “Always Show Nameplates” option being unchecked. With an addon like Plater, you can create a profile that only displays nameplates for your current target.

### 3\. My nameplates are overlapping and creating a mess. What can I do?

The Blizzard interface doesn’t offer much in the way of overlap control. Addons like **Plater** or **Threat Plates** can dynamically adjust nameplate positions to prevent overlap, ensuring readability. Explore their settings for “stacking” or “overlap” options.

### 4\. Can I change the color of nameplates based on threat level?

Yes! This is a common feature in addons like **Threat Plates**.
You can configure the addon to display nameplates in different colors depending on whether you have aggro, are about to lose aggro, or are not generating any threat.

### 5\. How do I restore my nameplate settings to default if I’ve messed them up?

The easiest way is to reset your entire UI. Click the Menu button in the lower left corner, select System, and then at the bottom of the pane, select **Reset User Options** and click “Okay”. Now log back into the game.

### 6\. What are the most common nameplate addons used by top players?

**Plater Nameplates** and **Threat Plates** are the two most popular by far. Some players also use variations or lightweight addons to tweak specific aspects of nameplate behavior.

### 7\. How can I report a player with an inappropriate name?

If you see a name that violates Blizzard’s naming guidelines, use the right-click option in-game to report it.
